feed.title: NPR Topics: Business
feed.subtitle: Find the latest business news with reports on Wall Street, interest rates, banking, companies, and U.S. and world financial markets. Subscribe to the Business Story of the Day podcast.

entry.title: Made in America: How AI is keeping this U.S. factory competitive
entry.summary: GE Appliances is leaning heavily into artificial intelligence to improve quality and efficiency on the factory floor.

entry.title: Kalshi bans former congressman George Santos for life after State of the Union trades
entry.summary: Kalshi says Santos did not cooperate with its investigation into bets he placed on his own attendance at the State of the Union. The company also fined the disgraced congressman more than $71,000.

entry.title: The U.S. sues Amazon again
entry.summary: Federal regulators and 22 states allege that the tech giant made billions by manipulating how much brands and sellers paid for ads on its platform.

entry.title: How a comic book store got swept into the tariff storm
entry.summary: Tariffs continue to rile all kinds of American businesses more than a year after Trump unveiled his first set of tariffs — including a comic book store owner in Ohio.

entry.title: Social media restrictions on young users: What do the kids say?
entry.summary: We've heard from adults about the new Facebook and Instagram rules, but what are kids saying? Teenage social media users talk about whether the proposed restrictions will have any effect on them.

entry.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
entry.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to fighting inflation in a major speech — raising expectations that rate hikes may be coming, though he did not clearly spell out a path going forward.

entry.title: U.S. says pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant. Energy experts disagree
entry.summary: Treasure Secretary Scott Bessent said oil pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant in two years. Energy experts say that is unlikely to happen.

entry.title: Businesses are getting tariff refunds. Why aren't consumers getting their cut?
entry.summary: A slew of American companies are getting billions of dollars back in tariff refunds after a Supreme Court ruling. Many consumers, though, may never get anything back.

entry.title: The stakes are high as Kevin Warsh is set to give his first major speech as Fed Chair
entry.summary: The stakes are high as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh prepares to give a speech on Friday at the annual gathering of economists and central bankers in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.

entry.title: School districts face a back-to-school math problem: The high price of diesel
entry.summary: With the war in Iran driving up fuel prices, diesel is now nearly $5.60 a gallon, affecting school districts at the start of the year.
